about: Xbox Achievement Unlocked is the familiar green Xbox notification: a round trophy badge on the left pops up and the pill-shaped banner slides out with the words "Achievement unlocked". On a console the line beneath would name an in-game accomplishment and its gamerscore. In the meme it instead names a tiny victory from real life, such as replying to an email the same day, cooking without setting off the smoke alarm, or remembering a coworker's name, celebrating it with the full ceremony of a video game reward. The more embarrassingly small the feat, the funnier the triumphant pop-up looks.
origin: Achievements arrived on Xbox 360 in 2005, and the notification pop-up quickly became shorthand for celebrating any small win, in games or out of them.
usage:
There is one text box, under the "Achievement unlocked" line inside the banner. Write the achievement as a short title or past-tense sentence, like a real in-game trophy. You can add a gamerscore value for flavor ("G 5").

Ideal achievements are mundane or slightly sad: adulting basics, social survival, personal records that are not really records. Keep it to one line so it fits the banner, and phrase it plainly, since deadpan matches the dry tone of real achievement descriptions.
ideas: Replied to an email on the same day
Cooked without setting off the smoke alarm
Survived a family dinner with no arguments
